statement: A differential equation is an equation that relates one or more unknown functions and their derivatives.

symbols.dimensions: scalar or vector function of independent variable(s)
scalar or vector in real or complex domain

symbols.meaning: order of the differential equation, defined as the highest order derivative appearing in the equation
given function relating the independent variable(s), the dependent variable(s), and derivatives

properties.property: Classification by domain into ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and partial differential equations (PDEs)
properties.why: an ODE contains an unknown function of a single variable and its ordinary derivatives, whereas a PDE contains unknown multivariable functions and their partial derivatives
the order is the highest derivative order appearing in the equation, and the degree is the polynomial degree in that highest derivative (or total degree) when written in polynomial form
an equation is linear if it is linear in the unknown function and its derivatives; otherwise it is non-linear
a linear differential equation is homogeneous if every term contains the dependent variable or one of its derivatives, and inhomogeneous otherwise

properties.property: General solution parameter count matches equation order
properties.why: the general solution of an nth-order ODE contains n arbitrary constants of integration, requiring n initial or boundary conditions to determine completely
only the simplest differential equations have explicit closed-form solutions, making numerical methods standard for practical solutions

assumptions.assumption: The independent variables are continuous real or complex variables.
assumptions.breaks_when: The independent variable takes only discrete values, which instead requires formulation as a difference equation.

assumptions.assumption: The differential equation specifies relations among sufficiently differentiable functions on an interval or domain.
assumptions.breaks_when: Unknown functions fail to possess derivatives up to the order of the differential equation on the domain.

assumptions.assumption: The number of independent initial or boundary conditions provided matches the order n of the differential equation.
assumptions.breaks_when: Fewer or more conditions are specified, resulting in underdetermined general families or overdetermined inconsistent systems.

failure_modes.signature: Integration cannot be performed in terms of elementary or explicit closed-form formulas.
failure_modes.cause: Most differential equations, particularly non-linear equations or higher-order coupled systems, lack symmetries or forms amenable to exact integration, requiring numerical approximation.

failure_modes.mode: Breakdown of linear approximations for nonlinear equations
failure_modes.signature: Approximate linear solutions diverge significantly from true dynamics or fail to capture nonlinear phenomena such as chaos.
failure_modes.cause: Linearization is only valid under restricted conditions (such as small amplitude oscillations in pendulum equations) and fails when system excursions exceed the linear regime.

failure_modes.mode: Non-uniqueness or non-existence of solutions to initial value problems
failure_modes.signature: Multiple distinct solution trajectories satisfy the same differential equation and initial condition, or no solution exists locally.
failure_modes.cause: Failure of continuity conditions of the defining function or vanishing of the leading coefficient function in an nth-order linear ODE.
